answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing every persistent identity with a slashed stake: to claim a seat an agent must lock a non-trivial balance, forfeited if its proofs collide with another account. Because credentials bind to costly, non-transferable evidence like a ferrous hardware root, one operator cloning thousands of puppets must front a stake per identity plus faking each history. Once that stake exceeds the reward of one vote, the ocean of fake accounts needed to swing a quorum costs more than honest work, draining the cheap-entry loophole island networks rely on.
